福爾摩沙小導遊臺南 Tainan・安平區

王雞屎洋樓與西㡣殿Wang Ji Shi Mansion & Xilong Temple

老安平最豪華的宅邸，主人的名字叫「雞屎」：王雞屎。七個姐姐接連夭折，父母給么兒取了卑賤的名字，盼望邪祟放過他。年輕時，他在安平運河與安平港之間擺渡載客。大日本製鹽株式會社的主管見他老實，把運鹽工作交給他，他因此致富。他請沒工作的工人吃飯、造橋鋪路，還辦流水席請全村吃飯。他死後被奉為土地公。洋樓建於 1937 年。找找門上白色的「O」──那是「王」的日語發音。隔壁的西㡣殿建於 1738 年，廟名用了一個罕見的「龍」字古字。廟裡找一尊約二十公分高、叼著近三十公分長菸斗的小神像，那就是王雞屎。從 2009 年起，廟方每天為他點一支菸。

The most luxurious mansion in old Anping belonged to a man whose name means chicken droppings: Wang Ji-Shi. His seven older sisters died one after another, so his parents gave him a lowly name, hoping evil spirits would leave him alone. As a young man, he ferried passengers between the Anping Canal and the harbor. Managers of the Dai-Nippon Salt Corporation saw how honest he was and gave him the salt-transport business. It made him rich. He fed workers who found no work, built bridges, paved roads, and threw free banquets for the whole village. After his death, he was enshrined as a Tudigong, a local earth god. His mansion was built in 1937. Look for the white letter O above the door: it is the Japanese sound of the name Wang. Next door is the Xilong Temple, founded in 1738. Its name uses a rare, ancient form of the word dragon. Inside, find a small statue about 20 centimeters tall with a pipe nearly 30 centimeters long. That is Wang Ji-Shi. Since 2009, the temple keepers light a cigarette for him every day.

One-minute intro

為什麼值得來

Why it matters & history

王雞屎洋樓是老安平最氣派的宅邸。主人王雞屎從擺渡起家，靠運鹽致富後樂善好施，死後被奉為土地公；隔壁西㡣殿裡，至今還有一尊叼著長菸斗的小神像。

The Wang mansion was the grandest house in old Anping. Its owner began as a ferryman, grew rich carrying salt, gave generously to his neighbors, and after his death was honored as a local earth god.

  1. 1738西㡣殿建廟，廟名用了「龍」字的古字。Xilong Temple is built, its name using an old form of the character for dragon.
  2. 日治時期 Japanese era王雞屎替製鹽會社運鹽而致富，造橋鋪路、辦流水席請村民吃飯。Wang grows rich hauling salt and pays for bridges, roads and village feasts.
  3. 1937洋樓落成，門上白色的「O」是「王」的日語發音。The mansion is completed; the white O on the door stands for the Japanese reading of Wang.
  4. 2009廟方認出叼菸斗的小神像就是王雞屎，此後每天為他點一支菸。The temple identifies the small pipe-holding statue as Wang and starts lighting a cigarette for him each day.

認識景點

About the place

豪宅、洋樓：又大又氣派的房子；王家洋樓建於 1937 年。 平房：只有一層樓的房子；洋樓的前棟是平房。 裝飾藝術風格：強調垂直與水平線條的幾何風格；窗子像算盤珠。 瀝青：黑色黏稠的材料；二戰時用它把高樓塗黑，躲避轟炸。

mansion: A large, fine house. Wang's mansion was built in 1937. bungalow: A house with only one floor. The front part of the mansion is a bungalow. Art Deco: A style with strong straight lines and simple shapes. The windows look like abacus beads. asphalt: A black, sticky material. In World War Two, the tall building was painted black to hide it from bombers.

壓艙石：讓船穩定的重石；在安平被拿來當石階和座椅。 擺渡：用船載人過水；年輕的王雞屎以擺渡維生。 運鹽：包裝與運送鹽；日治時期他靠這門生意致富。 鹽田：海邊一格格的淺池；引進海水，靠太陽曬成鹽。

ballast stone: A heavy stone that kept old ships steady. In Anping they became steps and seats. ferry: To carry people across water by boat. Young Wang ferried passengers. salt transport: Packing and carrying salt. This business made him rich under Japanese rule. salt field: Flat ponds by the sea. Seawater goes in, and the sun turns it into salt.

蒸發：水變成水氣跑掉；鹽就留了下來。 結晶：有平平切面的小硬塊；鹽的結晶是小方塊。 專賣：只有一個單位（例如政府）能掌控某種買賣；1899 年臺灣實施鹽的專賣。 慈善團體：募集金錢和人力、幫助需要的人的團體；王雞屎就像一人慈善團體。

evaporate: When water evaporates, it turns into air and goes away. The salt stays behind. crystal: A tiny hard piece with flat sides. Salt crystals are little cubes. monopoly: When only one group, like the government, controls a trade. In 1899, salt became a monopoly in Taiwan. charity: A group that collects money and help for people in need. Wang Ji-Shi was a one-man charity.

土地公：守護地方的土地神；王雞屎被奉為土地公。 奉為神明：死後被當成神明供奉。 菸斗：抽菸用的管子；王雞屎的小神像拿著很長的菸斗。 乩童：替神明傳話的人；2009 年乩童指出這尊神像就是王雞屎。

Tudigong: A local earth god. Wang Ji-Shi was enshrined as a Tudigong. be deified: To be worshipped as a god after death. pipe: A tube for smoking. Wang's little statue holds a very long pipe. spirit medium: A person who speaks for the gods. In 2009, the medium said the statue was Wang Ji-Shi.

異體字：同一個字的另一種寫法；廟名用了「龍」的古字。 境主神、守護神：守護一個地方的神；西㡣殿是「王城西」社的境主廟。

variant character: Another way to write the same character. The plaque uses an ancient form of dragon. guardian deity: A god who protects a neighborhood. Xilong Temple guards the area west of the King's Castle.

實景照片

Photos on site

王雞屎洋樓 Wang Ji Shi Mansion

王雞屎洋樓建於 1937 年，用洗石子做牆柱。看山頭中央的圓形徽飾，裡面有個白色的「O」，是日文「王」的發音。王家後代還住在這裡，請在外面安靜參觀。

Wang Ji Shi Mansion was built in 1937, with washed-pebble walls and columns. In the round medallion at the top is a white letter O, the Japanese sound of the name Wang. The family still lives here, so please look quietly from outside.

西龍殿 Xilong Temple

西龍殿主祀池府千歲，王雞屎的小神像也供奉在廟裡。屋頂上擠滿五顏六色的人物和龍；這兩塊匾額寫的是常見的「龍」字。

Xilong Temple's principal deity is Lord Chi, and Wang Ji Shi's little statue is kept inside. The roof is crowded with colorful figures and dragons. These two plaques use the everyday character for dragon.

西龍殿裡的王雞屎神像 Wang Ji Shi's statue

西龍殿神桌上這尊小神像，相傳就是王雞屎：戴著帽子、拿著長長的煙管，旁邊還放著一匹馬和一個菸灰缸，裡面有信徒供的香菸。

This small statue on the altar of Xilong Temple is said to be Wang Ji Shi. He wears a cap and holds a long pipe. Beside him are a horse and an ashtray with cigarettes left by worshippers.

王家後棟洋樓 The Wang family's rear building

這是王家 1937 年洋樓的後棟，一棟二層樓房：屋頂邊的女兒牆上有圓形徽飾和花草浮雕，窗戶上有窗楣。王家後代還住在這裡，請在外面安靜參觀。

This is the rear building of the Wang family's 1937 mansion, a two-storey house with a round medallion and carved flowers along the top. The family still lives here, so please look quietly from outside.
